column2: top-reviewer aggregation still prefers flat `review-findings-full.jsonl` counts whenever `findings_file` is populated, and `render_phase_detail` only calls `_top_reviewers_from_classification` under a design-only gate (often only when jsonl is absent). `/implement` runs usually have jsonl present, so weighted `findings-classification.tsv` aggregation never runs for implement progress output even when every round has classification data; operators see flat +1 top reviewers while tally scoreboards may show weighted points.

the planned high-severity (+2) rule conflicts across wording and edge cases: strict consensus vs strict majority of non-empty ratings vs missing/invalid ratings returning ordinary +1. mixed panels (e.g. 2-high/1-ordinary, 1-high/2-missing, or 2 yes minor + 1 no major) have no single verifiable expected score. the helper does not specify whether no-voter severities enter the denominator.

classification-only scoring cannot distinguish code-review oos `finding_n` rows (including legacy `### finding_n: [out_of_scope]` accepted findings with major panel severity) from in-scope rows. tsv scoring only skips `oos_` prefixes, so such rows are emitted as `finding_n` without a scope marker and can receive in-scope +2 instead of flat oos +1 or exclusion.

code-review `reviewer_slots` are pipe-delimited (`cursor-a-output.txt|codex-b-output.txt`), but the proposed tsv attribution path does not specify splitting on `|`. weighted classification scoreboards or top reviewers that comma-split will credit one synthetic reviewer and violate equal point-sharing for co-reviewers.

the plan extends `score_rows` with an accepted-point weight but does not replace score formulas that still sum unweighted accepted/oos-accepted counts minus rejections. in `plan_review_tally._scoreboard` (and the parallel inline scoreboard in `review_tally.py`), `plan_review_tally._render` never collects voter severities before scoring, and `review_tally` ignores `vn_severity` in cells during aggregation. high-severity accepted in-scope findings still score +1 and the weighted feature does not ship.

`_top_reviewers_from_classification` / `_accepted_reviewers_from_classification` append one reviewer name per accepted row (+1 each) and do not read `v1_severity`/`v2_severity`/`v3_severity`. even after routing is fixed, top reviewers would count findings not weighted points; a major-consensus row ranks the same as a minor row while tally scoreboards show +2.

the plan omits reviewer-facing competition notice updates. code review and plan review prompts (`python/rendering.py`, `skills/design/references/plan-review.md`) still tell reviewers every accepted finding earns +1, contradicting value-weighted scoring and weakening the stated incentive change.
